questions.stem:
Owning a pet is a lifetime of commitment (up to ten years or
more if you own a dog or a cat) involving considerable
responsibility. The decision to acquire one, therefore, should
be made by the whole family. Without full agreement by
everyone, the pet could end up unwanted. Puppies and
kittens are so adorable, it is easy to understand why adults
and children alike would be attracted to them.

Your neighbour is tempted to buy a puppy the moment he sees one, and he has not asked anyone else in the house; according to the passage, what is likely to happen? (A) The whole family will share the work of looking after it (B) The family may fail to agree and the pet could end up unwanted (C) Everyone in the house will be attracted to it as soon as it is bought (D) The decision to buy it will be left to the person who brings it home

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The family may fail to agree and the pet could end up unwanted

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: The Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals in your city has offered you its centre board for a display. Write a notice of about 100 words for that board, headed NOTICE, giving a heading, telling readers what owning a pet involves, listing what must be arranged or done before a puppy is taken home, and closing with the name of the Society.

markingPoints.description: Content: states that owning a pet is a lifetime of commitment, up to ten years or more if you own a dog or a cat, and that the decision to acquire one must be made by the whole family.

Content: lists at least four of the requirements — an annual dog licence in accordance with government regulations, annual vaccination against major diseases, toilet training, obedience training, a balanced diet, socialisation, and a daily dose of exercise, affection and play.
Format: opens with the word NOTICE, carries a heading, and closes with the name of the Society, as a notice board notice must.
Organisation: the points run as short clear lines in an order a reader can take in at once.
Accuracy and expression: correct spelling and punctuation, a polite and practical style, and a total of about 100 words.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
NOTICE

Points to Remember Before Adopting a Puppy

The Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals reminds everyone that a pet is a lifetime of commitment, up to ten years or more if you own a dog or a cat, and that the decision to acquire one must be made by the whole family. Every owner must also arrange an annual dog licence in accordance with government regulations, annual vaccination against major diseases, toilet training, obedience training, a balanced diet, socialisation and a daily dose of exercise, affection and play.

Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: You have decided to bring the otter you acquired from the Tigris marshes all the way back to Camusfearna. Write a letter of about 100 words to a friend giving the whole travel plan and telling him what has already been done to make the journey safe.

markingPoints.description: Content: states that the British airline to London will not fly animals, so a flight to Paris has been booked on another airline, with London to be reached from there.
Content: states that the airline insists the otter be packed into a box not more than eighteen inches square, to be carried on the floor at the writer’s feet.
Content: mentions that a box has been made and the otter put into it an hour before the start so that he would become accustomed to it.
Format: begins with a greeting, and closes with a formal sign-off and the writer’s name, as a letter must.
Organisation and accuracy: the plan is given in a clear order, with correct spelling, punctuation and a total of about 100 words.

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Dear friend,

Good news. The otter is with me and we are leaving for England shortly. The British airline to London will not fly animals, so I have booked a flight to Paris on another airline, and shall travel on to London from there. The airline insists that Mij should be packed into a box not more than eighteen inches square, to be carried on the floor at my feet. I have had a box made, and an hour before we start I shall put him into it so that he will become accustomed to it.

Yours sincerely,
Gavin Maxwell

and an hour before we started, I put Mij into the
box so that he would become accustomed to it, and
left for a hurried meal.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is holding an assembly on the animals in our lives, and you have been chosen to speak. Write a speech of about 100 words for the assembly, greeting everyone, saying what owning a pet actually involves, and saying what owners must never do to a dog and must always do for it.

markingPoints.description: Content: states that owning a pet is a lifetime of commitment, up to ten years or more if you own a dog or a cat, and that it involves considerable responsibility.
Content: says that keeping dogs confined in cages or tying them up to stop them dirtying the garden or chewing on shoes is wrong.

Content: says that socialisation is very important, and that a pet needs a balanced diet, a daily dose of exercise, affection and play, and that reading up on the subject beforehand is an important requirement.
Format: opens with a greeting to the assembly and closes with a formal thank you, as a speech must.
Organisation and accuracy: the points are set out in an order the audience can follow, with correct spelling, punctuation and a total of about 100 words.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Good morning, everyone. Many of us have wanted a puppy or a kitten at some time. But owning a pet is a lifetime of commitment, up to ten years or more if you own a dog or a cat, and it involves considerable responsibility. So remember two things today. First, never confine a dog in a cage or tie it up to stop it dirtying the garden or chewing on shoes; that is wrong, and socialisation is very important. Second, give your pet a balanced diet and a daily dose of exercise, affection and play, and read up on the subject beforehand. Thank you.

evidence:
• socialisation (many dogs are kept confined in cages or tied
up to stop them from dirtying the garden or from chewing
on shoes — this is wrong) is very important
• don’t forget you should feed your pet a balanced diet
• a daily dose of exercise, affection and play.

questions.stem: Set out in steps what Maxwell found when he came back from his hurried meal, and how he still got the otter onto the waiting aeroplane.

markingPoints.description: An hour before the flight Maxwell had put Mij into the box so that he would become accustomed to it, and left for a hurried meal.
On his return the box was silent, but blood had trickled and dried from its airholes and chinks around the lid.
He whipped off the lock and tore open the lid, and Mij, exhausted and blood-spattered, whimpered at his leg.
Mij had torn the box lining to shreds, and Maxwell removed it so that no cutting edges were left.
It was just ten minutes to the flight and the airport was five miles distant, so he put Mij back and held down the lid.
The driver tore through the streets of Basra, and he was rushed to the waiting aircraft by infuriated officials.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Trace in steps the change in the otter’s behaviour from his first aloof hours to the games he discovered with water and with the taps.

markingPoints.description: For the first twenty-four hours Mijbil was neither hostile nor friendly, but aloof and indifferent, sleeping on the floor as far from Maxwell’s bed as possible.
On the second night he came on to the bed and stayed asleep in the crook of Maxwell’s knees.
During the day he lost his apathy and took a keen interest in his surroundings.
On a lead he went wild with joy in the bathroom, plunging and rolling in the water.
Maxwell learnt that every drop of water must be spread about the place, and a bowl must be overturned or sat in until it overflows.
Two days later he turned a chromium tap with his paws, and later screwed it up tighter, chittering at the tap’s failure to cooperate.
